title.zh: 卷271 列傳五十八 徐乾学 王鸿绪 高士奇
title.en: Volume 271 Biographies 58: Xu Qianxue, Wang Hongxu, Gao Shiqi
title.raw: 卷271 列傳五十八 徐乾学 王鸿绪 高士奇

sentences.zh: 列傳五十八

translations.literal: Biographies 58
translations.idiomatic: Biography 58

sentences.zh: 徐-{乾}-學，字原一，江南崑山人。

translations.literal: Xu Qianxue, styled Yuanyi, was a native of Kunshan in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Qianxue, whose style name was Yuanyi, came from Kunshan in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 幼慧，八歳能文。

translations.literal: As a child he was clever; at eight sui he could compose literary pieces.
translations.idiomatic: He was precocious as a boy and could write essays by the age of eight.

sentences.zh: 康熙九年，一甲三名進士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kangxi he placed third among the first-rank jinshi graduates and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1670 he took third place among the top three jinshi and was made a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 十一年，副蔡啓僔主順天鄕試，拔韓菼-{於}-遺巻中，明年魁天下，文體一變。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he served as associate examiner under Cai Qipu for the Shuntian provincial examination, selecting Han Tan from among the rejected papers; the next year Han topped the metropolitan examination and literary style changed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In 1672 he assisted Cai Qipu in supervising the Shuntian provincial exams and picked Han Tan from the discarded papers; Han came in first nationwide the following year, and examination prose was transformed from that point on.

sentences.zh: 坐副榜未取漢軍巻，與啓僔-{並}-鐫秩調用。

translations.literal: Because on the supplementary list he had not admitted the Bannermen papers, he and Qipu were both demoted in rank and transferred.
translations.idiomatic: He and Qipu were both stripped of rank and reassigned for having failed to pass any Han Military Banner candidates on the supplementary list.

sentences.zh: 尋-{復}-故官，遷左贊善，充日講起居注官。

translations.literal: Before long he was restored to his former post, promoted to Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent, and appointed Daily Lecturer and Recorder of the Emperor's Actions.
translations.idiomatic: He soon regained his former office, was made Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent, and served as Daily Lecturer and Recorder of the Emperor's Actions.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂歸，-{乾}-學父先卒，哀毀三年，喪葬一以禮；

translations.literal: On entering mourning for his mother he returned home; Qianxue's father had died earlier, and for three years he grieved with destructive fervor and conducted the funeral entirely according to ritual;
translations.idiomatic: He went home to observe mourning for his mother; his father had already died, and for three years he mourned with extreme grief and conducted the funeral wholly by the rites;

sentences.zh: 及母卒，如之。

translations.literal: when his mother died he did the same.
translations.idiomatic: when his mother died he did likewise.

sentences.zh: 爲讀禮通考百二十巻，博採衆説，剖析其義。

translations.literal: He compiled one hundred and twenty juan of Comprehensive Studies on the Reading of Ritual, broadly gathering many schools' views and analyzing their meaning.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Comprehensive Studies on the Reading of Ritual in 120 juan, drawing widely on scholarly opinions and parsing their significance.

sentences.zh: 服闋，起故官。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he resumed his former office.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period he returned to his former post.

sentences.zh: 充明史總裁官，累遷侍講學士。

translations.literal: He served as chief compiler of the History of the Ming and was repeatedly promoted to Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed chief compiler of the History of the Ming and rose step by step to Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，-{乾}-學弟元文以左都-{御}-史降調，其子樹聲與-{乾}-學子樹屛-{並}-舉順天鄕試。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year Qianxue's younger brother Yuanwen was demoted from Left Censor-in-Chief, and Yuanwen's son Shusheng and Qianxue's son Shuping both passed the Shuntian provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1684 his younger brother Xu Yuanwen was demoted from Left Censor-in-Chief, while Yuanwen's son Shusheng and Qianxue's son Shuping both passed the Shuntian provincial exams.

sentences.zh: 上以是科取中南皿巻皆江、浙人，而湖廣、江西、福建無一與者，下九卿科道磨勘。

translations.literal: Because all those admitted from the southern examination rolls in this session were from Jiangsu and Zhejiang, while Hunan-Guangdong, Jiangxi, and Fujian had not a single candidate, the emperor ordered the Nine Ministers and the censorate and surveillance offices to conduct a rigorous review.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor found that every candidate admitted from the southern rolls that year came from Jiangsu or Zhejiang, with none from Hunan-Guangdong, Jiangxi, or Fujian, and ordered a full review by the Nine Ministers and the censorate.

sentences.zh: 樹屛等坐斥舉人。

translations.literal: Shuping and others were punished by dismissal of their licentiate status.
translations.idiomatic: Shuping and the others were stripped of their status as licentiates.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，-{乾}-學進詹事。

translations.literal: That winter Qianxue was promoted to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，召試翰詹諸臣，擢-{乾}-學第一，與侍讀韓菼、編修孫-{岳}-頒、侍講歸允肅、編修喬萊等四人-{並}-降敕褒獎賞賚。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year the Hanlin and Grand Secretariat officials were summoned for examination; Qianxue was ranked first, and together with Reader Han Tan, Compiler Sun Yuebin, Lecturer Gui Yunsu, Compiler Qiao Lai, and three others he received an imperial edict of commendation and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: In 1685 the emperor tested the Hanlin and Grand Secretariat corps and ranked Qianxue first; he and Han Tan, Sun Yuebin, Gui Yunsu, Qiao Lai, and three others were all rewarded by imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 尋直南書房，擢内閣學士，充大淸會典、一統-{志}-副總裁，教習庶吉士。

translations.literal: Soon he served in the Southern Study, was promoted to Grand Secretariat academician, served as associate chief compiler of the Great Qing Statutes and the Unified Gazetteer, and instructed junior compilers.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon assigned to the Southern Study, made a Grand Secretariat academician, named associate chief compiler of the Great Qing Statutes and the Unified Gazetteer, and put in charge of instructing junior compilers.

sentences.zh: 時戸部郎中色楞額往福建稽察鼓鑄，請禁用明代舊錢，尚書科爾坤、-{餘}-國柱等議如所請。

translations.literal: At the time Ministry of Revenue department director Selengge went to Fujian to inspect coin casting and requested prohibition of Ming-dynasty old coin; Ministers Korhün and Yu Guozhu and others deliberated in favor of the request.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Selengge of the Ministry of Revenue was inspecting minting in Fujian and asked to ban Ming-era coin; Ministers Korhün and Yu Guozhu endorsed his proposal.

sentences.zh: -{乾}-學言：「自古皆新舊兼行，以從民便。

translations.literal: Qianxue said: "From antiquity new and old coin have always circulated together for the people's convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Qianxue argued: "Throughout history old and new currency have circulated side by side for public convenience.

sentences.zh: 若設厲禁，恐滋紛擾。

translations.literal: If harsh prohibitions are set up, I fear disorder will increase."
translations.idiomatic: Harsh prohibition would only breed unrest."

sentences.zh: 」因考自漢至明故事，爲議以獻。

translations.literal: He therefore researched precedents from Han through Ming and submitted a memorial with his opinion.
translations.idiomatic: He researched precedents from the Han through the Ming and submitted a memorial setting out his view.

sentences.zh: 上然之，事遂寢。

translations.literal: The emperor approved it, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, and the proposal was shelved.

sentences.zh: 詔採購遺書，-{乾}-學以宋、元經解、李燾續通-{鑑}-長編及唐開元禮，或繕寫，或仍古本，綜其體要，條列奏進，上稱善。

translations.literal: An edict ordered procurement of lost books; Qianxue presented Song and Yuan commentaries on the classics, Li Tao's Continuation of the Comprehensive Mirror in several long compilations, and the Tang Kaiyuan Rites—some copied anew, some in ancient editions—summarized their essentials in listed form and memorialized them; the emperor praised them.
translations.idiomatic: When the court ordered the purchase of rare books, Qianxue submitted Song and Yuan classical commentaries, Li Tao's Continuation of the Comprehensive Mirror, and the Tang Kaiyuan Rites, some freshly copied and some in old editions, with a summary of each work's main points; the emperor commended the selection.

sentences.zh: 時-{乾}-學與學士張英日侍左右，凡著作之任，皆以屬之。

translations.literal: At the time Qianxue and Academician Zhang Ying attended daily at the emperor's side, and all literary tasks were entrusted to them.
translations.idiomatic: Qianxue and Academician Zhang Ying then attended the emperor daily, and every literary commission was given to them.

sentences.zh: 學士例推巡撫，​​上以二人學問淹通，宜侍從，特諭吏部，遇巡撫缺勿預推。

translations.literal: Academicians were routinely nominated for provincial governorships, but the emperor, considering the two men's learning broad and penetrating and fit for attendance, specially instructed the Ministry of Personnel that when governorships fell vacant they should not be put forward.
translations.idiomatic: Academicians were usually put forward as provincial governors, but the emperor, judging both men's scholarship too valuable to lose from court, told the Ministry of Personnel not to nominate them for such posts.

sentences.zh: 未-{幾}-，遷禮部侍郎，直講經筵。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites and lectured directly at the Classics Colloquium.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made Vice Minister of Rites and lectured at the Classics Colloquium.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮使臣鄭載-{嵩}-訴其國王受枉，語悖妄。

translations.literal: The Korean envoy Zheng Zaisong complained that his king had been wronged, his words rebellious and reckless.
translations.idiomatic: The Korean envoy Zheng Zaisong petitioned that his king had been treated unjustly, speaking in insolent and extravagant terms.

sentences.zh: -{乾}-學謂恐長外籓跋扈，劾其使臣失辭不敬，宜責以大義。

translations.literal: Qianxue said he feared this would encourage outer vassals to grow overbearing; he impeached the envoy for improper and disrespectful speech and urged that he be rebuked with the great moral principles.
translations.idiomatic: Qianxue warned that such language would encourage tributary states to grow arrogant, impeached the envoy for disrespectful speech, and urged that he be lectured on proper relations with the throne.

sentences.zh: 上見疎，獎，謂有關國體。

translations.literal: The emperor saw the memorial, praised it, and said it concerned the dignity of the state.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial, praised it, and said it touched the honor of the empire.

sentences.zh: 已而王上疎謝罪。

translations.literal: Before long the Korean king submitted a memorial of apology.
translations.idiomatic: The Korean king soon submitted a memorial of apology.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，遷左都-{御}-史，擢刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was transferred to Left Censor-in-Chief and promoted to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In 1687 he became Left Censor-in-Chief and was promoted to Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，典會試。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he presided over the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1688 he served as chief examiner for the metropolitan civil service examination.

sentences.zh: 初，明珠當國，勢張甚，其黨布中外，-{乾}-學不能立異同。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Songgotu held power, his influence was greatly extended and his faction spread inside and outside the court; Qianxue could not stand apart with a different view.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Songgotu dominated the government, his faction was everywhere and Qianxue could not afford to oppose him openly.

sentences.zh: 至是，明珠漸失帝眷，而-{乾}-學驟拜左都-{御}-史，即劾罷江西巡撫安世鼎，諷諸-{御}-史風聞言事，-{臺}-諫多所彈劾，不避權貴。

translations.literal: By then Songgotu was gradually losing imperial favor, while Qianxue was suddenly appointed Left Censor-in-Chief; he immediately impeached and removed Jiangxi Governor An Shiding, hinted to the censors to report on hearsay, and the surveillance and remonstrance offices impeached many without avoiding the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: By then Songgotu was falling from favor, and Qianxue, suddenly made Left Censor-in-Chief, at once impeached Jiangxi Governor An Shiding, urged the censors to speak on rumor and report, and the surveillance offices brought down many charges without sparing the powerful.

sentences.zh: 明珠竟罷相，衆皆謂-{乾}-學主之。

translations.literal: Songgotu was finally dismissed from the premiership, and everyone said Qianxue had masterminded it.
translations.idiomatic: Songgotu was finally removed from office, and the court widely credited Qianxue.

sentences.zh: 時有南、北黨之目，互相抨撃。

translations.literal: At the time there were labels of Southern and Northern factions, attacking each other.
translations.idiomatic: The court then spoke of Southern and Northern factions and their mutual attacks.

sentences.zh: 尚書科爾坤、佛倫，明珠黨也，-{乾}-學遇會議會推，輒與齟。

translations.literal: Ministers Korhün and Folun were of Songgotu's faction; whenever Qianxue met them in joint deliberation or nomination conferences he clashed with them.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers Korhün and Folun belonged to Songgotu's party, and Qianxue invariably clashed with them in joint conferences and nomination meetings.

sentences.zh: 總河靳輔奏下河屯田，下九卿會議，-{乾}-學偕尚書張玉書言屯田所佔民地應歸舊業，科爾坤、佛倫勿從。

translations.literal: Director-General of Rivers Jin Fu memorialized on garrison farming in the lower Yellow River region; the matter was sent to the Nine Ministers for joint deliberation; Qianxue together with Minister Zhang Yushu said the civilian land occupied by the garrison farms should revert to its original holders; Korhün and Folun would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Fu, Director-General of Rivers, proposed garrison farming on the lower Yellow River; at the Nine Ministers' conference Qianxue and Zhang Yushu argued that civilian land taken for the farms should be restored, but Korhün and Folun dissented.

sentences.zh: -{御}-史陸祖修因劾科爾坤等偏袒河臣，不顧公議，-{御}-史郭琇亦劾輔興屯累民，詔罷輔任。

translations.literal: Censor Lu Zuxiu impeached Korhün and others for favoring the river official and disregarding public opinion; Censor Guo Xiu also impeached Fu for garrison farming that harmed the people; an edict removed Fu from office.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Lu Zuxiu charged Korhün and his allies with favoring the river chief against public opinion; Censor Guo Xiu charged Jin Fu with garrison farming that burdened the people, and the emperor dismissed Jin Fu.

sentences.zh: 湖廣巡撫張汧亦明珠私人，先是命色楞額往讞上荊南道祖澤深婪贓各款，-{並}-察汧有無穢跡，色楞額悉爲庇隱。

translations.literal: Huguang Governor Zhang Qian was also Songgotu's man; earlier Selengge had been ordered to Fujian to try the case of Jingnan Circuit intendant Zu Zeshen's greedy corruption on all counts and also to investigate whether Qian had any taint; Selengge concealed everything.
translations.idiomatic: Huguang Governor Zhang Qian was another of Songgotu's clients; Selengge had earlier been sent to try Circuit Intendant Zu Zeshen on charges of corruption and to investigate Zhang Qian as well, but Selengge covered everything up.

sentences.zh: -{御}-史陳紫芝劾汧貪黷，命副都-{御}-史開音布會巡撫-{於}-成龍、馬齊覆訊，汧、澤深事倶實，-{復}-得澤深交結大學士-{餘}-國柱爲囑色楞額徇庇及汧遣人赴京行賄狀，下法司嚴議。

translations.literal: Censor Chen Zizhi impeached Qian for greed and corruption; Vice Censor-in-Chief Kaiyinbu was ordered to join Governors Yu Chenglong and Ma Qi in re-examination; the cases against Qian and Zeshen were all substantiated, and it was further found that Zeshen had associated with Grand Secretary Yu Guozhu to ask Selengge to show favor and that Qian had sent men to the capital to offer bribes; the matter was sent to the judiciary for severe deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Chen Zizhi impeached Zhang Qian for corruption; Vice Censor-in-Chief Kaiyinbu joined Governors Yu Chenglong and Ma Qi in a reinvestigation that confirmed the charges against Zhang and Zu, and further showed that Zu had enlisted Grand Secretary Yu Guozhu to protect him through Selengge and that Zhang had sent agents to bribe officials in the capital; the judiciary was ordered to deliberate severely.

sentences.zh: 時國柱已爲琇劾罷，法司請檄追質訊，-{並}-詰汧行賄何人，汧指-{乾}-學。

translations.literal: By then Guozhu had already been impeached and removed by Xiu; the judiciary requested a summons for further interrogation and also asked whom Qian had bribed; Qian pointed to Qianxue.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Guozhu had already been impeached out of office by Guo Xiu; the judiciary asked to summon him for questioning and pressed Zhang Qian on whom he had bribed; Zhang named Qianxue.

sentences.zh: 上聞，命免國柱質訊，戒勿株連。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he ordered Guozhu exempted from interrogation and warned against implicating others.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard of it, exempted Yu Guozhu from interrogation, and warned against widening the net.

sentences.zh: -{於}-是但論汧、澤深、色楞額如律，事遂寢。

translations.literal: Thereupon only Qian, Zeshen, and Selengge were judged according to law, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Only Zhang Qian, Zu Zeshen, and Selengge were then punished under the law, and the affair ended there.

sentences.zh: -{乾}-學尋乞罷，疎言：「臣蒙特達之知，感激矢報，苞苴餽遺，一切禁絶。

translations.literal: Qianxue soon requested dismissal, memorializing: "Your servant has received extraordinary favor and is grateful to devote himself in return; gifts and presents of every kind I have entirely forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Qianxue soon asked to resign, writing: "Your servant has received extraordinary favor and is resolved to repay it; I have refused every gift and bribe offered to me.

sentences.zh: 前任湖北巡撫張汧橫肆汙衊，縁臣爲憲長，拒其幣問，是以銜憾誣攀。

translations.literal: The former Huguang Governor Zhang Qian behaved outrageously in slander; because your servant was chief of the surveillance commission and refused his gifts and inquiries, he bore a grudge and falsely implicated me.
translations.idiomatic: Former Huguang Governor Zhang Qian has slandered me outrageously because, as chief censor, I refused his gifts and visits, and he now bears a grudge and falsely implicates me.

sentences.zh: 非聖明在上，是非-{幾}-至混淆。

translations.literal: Had not the sage ruler been above, right and wrong would almost have been confused.
translations.idiomatic: Were it not for Your Majesty's clarity, truth and falsehood would nearly have been confused.

sentences.zh: 臣備位卿僚，乃爲貪吏誣構，皇上覆載之仁，不加譴責，臣-{復}-何顏出入禁廷，有玷淸班？

translations.literal: Your servant holds a place among ministers yet is framed by a greedy official; the emperor's all-encompassing benevolence has not imposed censure—yet with what face can your servant enter and leave the forbidden court and stain the pure ranks?
translations.idiomatic: I hold ministerial rank yet am framed by a corrupt official; Your Majesty's mercy has spared me punishment, yet how can I still walk the inner court without disgracing the pure service?

sentences.zh: 伏冀聖慈放歸田裡。

translations.literal: I humbly beg the sage compassion to release me to return to my fields."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty's compassion to let me return home."

sentences.zh: 」詔許以原官解任，仍領修書總裁事。

translations.literal: An edict permitted him to resign while retaining his original rank, and he still headed the chief compilation of books.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor allowed him to step down while keeping his rank and still directing the book-compilation projects.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，元文拜大學士，-{乾}-學子樹-{穀}-考選-{御}-史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year Yuanwen was appointed Grand Secretary, and Qianxue's son Shugu passed the censor selection examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1689 Yuanwen became Grand Secretary, and Qianxue's son Shugu was selected as a censor.

sentences.zh: 副都-{御}-史許三禮劾-{乾}-學：「律身不嚴，爲張汧所引。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Xu Sanli impeached Qianxue: "He does not discipline himself strictly and was implicated by Zhang Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Xu Sanli impeached Qianxue: "He has not kept himself in strict order and was named by Zhang Qian.

sentences.zh: 皇上寬仁，不加譴責，即宜引咎自退，乞命歸-{里}-。

translations.literal: The emperor has been lenient and did not impose censure; he should therefore take blame upon himself and withdraw, begging permission to return home.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor has been merciful and has not punished him; he ought to accept blame and withdraw, begging leave to go home.

sentences.zh: 又-{復}-優柔-{系}-戀，潛住長安。

translations.literal: Yet again he wavers and clings, secretly staying in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he lingers in indecision and secretly remains in the capital.

sentences.zh: 乘修史爲名，出入禁廷，與髙士奇相爲表裡。

translations.literal: Using book compilation as a pretext, he enters and leaves the forbidden court and acts inside and outside with Gao Shiqi.
translations.idiomatic: Under cover of historical compilation he comes and goes within the palace and works hand in glove with Gao Shiqi.

sentences.zh: 物議沸騰，招搖納賄。

translations.literal: Public criticism boils over; he solicits and accepts bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Public outrage is widespread, and he is accused of soliciting bribes.

sentences.zh: 其子樹-{穀}-不遵成例，朦朧考選-{御}-史，明有所恃。

translations.literal: His son Shugu did not follow established precedent and was obscurely passed in the censor selection examination, clearly relying on backing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shugu was irregularly passed in the censor selection, plainly counting on his father's protection.

sentences.zh: 獨其弟秉義文行兼優，原任禮部尚書熊賜履理學醇儒，乞立即召用，以佐盛治。

translations.literal: Only his younger brother Bingyi excels in both literary and conduct excellence; the former Minister of Rites Xiong Cilü is a pure Confucian of the Learning of Principle—I beg that both be immediately summoned to service to assist the flourishing rule.
translations.idiomatic: By contrast his younger brother Bingyi is outstanding in learning and conduct, and former Minister of Rites Xiong Cilü is a true scholar of Neo-Confucian principle; I beg that both be recalled at once to assist the flourishing reign.

sentences.zh: -{乾}-學當逐出史館，樹-{穀}-應調部屬，以遵成例。

translations.literal: Qianxue should be expelled from the Historiography Office; Shugu should be transferred to a ministry post to follow established precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Qianxue should be expelled from the Historiography Office and Shugu transferred to a regular ministry post in accordance with precedent."

sentences.zh: 」詔-{乾}-學-{復}-奏，-{乾}-學疎辨，乞罷斥歸田，-{並}-免樹-{穀}-職。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Qianxue to reply; Qianxue memorialized in defense, begging dismissal and return to the fields, and also requesting removal of Shugu from office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Qianxue to respond; Qianxue defended himself in a memorial, asked to be dismissed and sent home, and requested that Shugu be removed from office.

sentences.zh: 疎皆下部議，坐三禮所劾無實，應鐫秩調用。

translations.literal: The memorials were all sent to the ministries for deliberation; on the ground that Sanli's charges lacked substance, he should be demoted in rank and transferred.
translations.idiomatic: Both memorials went to the ministries for review, which found Sanli's charges unsubstantiated and recommended demotion and transfer.

sentences.zh: 三禮益恚，复列款訐-{乾}-學贓罪，帝嚴斥之，免降調，仍留任。

translations.literal: Sanli grew still more resentful and again listed items accusing Qianxue of corruption; the emperor sternly rebuked him, exempted the demotion and transfer, and Qianxue remained in post.
translations.idiomatic: Sanli, still angrier, renewed his charges of corruption against Qianxue; the emperor sharply rebuked him, set aside the recommended demotion, and kept Qianxue in office.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，-{乾}-學复上疎言：「臣年六十，精神衰耗，祗以受恩深重，依戀徘徊。

translations.literal: That winter Qianxue again memorialized: "Your servant is sixty years old, his spirit and strength declining; only because the favor received is so deep does he linger in attachment.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Qianxue memorialized again: "Your servant is sixty, my strength is failing, and I have lingered only because Your Majesty's favor has been so great.

sentences.zh: 三禮私怨逞忿，幸聖主洞燭幽隱。

translations.literal: Sanli vented private resentment; fortunately the sage ruler penetrated what was hidden.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Sanli pursued a private vendetta, but Your Majesty saw through his malice.

sentences.zh: 臣方寸靡-{寧}-，不能复事鉛槧。

translations.literal: Your servant's heart is without peace and cannot again attend to brush and ink.
translations.idiomatic: My mind is no longer at peace, and I cannot again devote myself to scholarship.

sentences.zh: 且恐因循居此，更有無端彈射。

translations.literal: Moreover I fear that if I linger here through inertia there will be further groundless impeachments.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that if I linger here, further groundless attacks will follow.

sentences.zh: 乞恩終始矜全，俾得保其衰病之身，歸省先臣丘隴，庶身心閒暇。

translations.literal: I beg grace from beginning to end in compassionate preservation, that I may preserve this declining and ailing body, return to visit my forefathers' mounds, and perhaps find leisure for body and mind.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty's mercy from first to last, that I may preserve my failing health, return to tend my parents' graves, and find some peace of body and mind.

sentences.zh: 原比古人書局自隨之義，屛跡編摩，少報萬一。

translations.literal: I wish to compare with the ancient meaning of carrying one's book office with one, retiring from sight to compile and edit, and repay one ten-thousandth."
translations.idiomatic: I ask to follow the ancient precedent of carrying one's editorial work home, retire from public life to compile books, and repay Your Majesty in the smallest measure."

sentences.zh: 」乃許給假回籍，降旨褒嘉，命攜書籍即家編輯。

translations.literal: He was then permitted leave to return to his native place; an edict of praise was issued, ordering him to take books home and edit there.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted him leave to return home, issued a commendatory edict, and ordered him to take his books and continue editing at home.

sentences.zh: 二十九年春，陛辭，賜-{御}-書「光焰萬丈」榜額。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-ninth year he took leave at court and was granted an imperial inscription reading "Radiance ten thousand zhang" as a plaque.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1690 he took leave at court and received an imperial plaque inscribed "Radiance of Ten Thousand Zhang."

sentences.zh: 未-{幾}-，兩江總督傅-{臘}-塔疎劾-{乾}-學囑-{託}-蘇州府貢監等請建生祠，复縱其子侄交結巡撫洪之傑，倚勢競利，請敕部嚴議。

translations.literal: Before long Liangjiang Governor-General Fu Latu memorialized impeaching Qianxue for having instructed Suzhou prefectural tribute students and others to request a living shrine, and again indulging his sons and nephews in associating with Governor Hong Zhijie to compete for profit by relying on power; he requested an edict to the ministries for severe deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Liangjiang Governor-General Fu Latu impeached Qianxue for arranging a living shrine through Suzhou tribute students and for letting his sons and nephews collude with Governor Hong Zhijie to profit from his influence, asking the ministries to deliberate severely.

sentences.zh: 語具元文傳。

translations.literal: The account is given in full in Yuanwen's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in Xu Yuanwen's biography.

sentences.zh: 上置弗問，而予元文休致。

translations.literal: The emperor set it aside without inquiry but granted Yuanwen retirement.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ignored the charges against Qianxue but allowed Yuanwen to retire.

sentences.zh: 三十年，山東巡撫佛倫劾濰縣知縣硃敦厚加收火耗論死，-{並}-及-{乾}-學嘗致書前任巡撫錢鎯庇敦厚。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year Shandong Governor Folun impeached Weixian Magistrate Zhu Dunhou for imposing extra melt-fees and sought the death penalty, also implicating Qianxue for having once written to the former governor Qian Yi to shield Dunhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1691 Shandong Governor Folun charged Weixian Magistrate Zhu Dunhou with illegal surcharges and sought his execution, also citing Qianxue's letter to former Governor Qian Yi shielding Zhu.

sentences.zh: -{乾}-學與鎯倶坐是奪職。

translations.literal: Qianxue and Yi were both punished by removal from office on this account.
translations.idiomatic: Qianxue and Qian Yi were both stripped of office on this charge.

sentences.zh: 自是齮齕者不已。

translations.literal: From then on those who gnawed at him did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: From then on his enemies never let up.

sentences.zh: 嘉定知縣聞在上爲縣民訐告私派，逮獄，閲二年未定讞。

translations.literal: Jiading Magistrate Wen Zaishang was impeached by county people for unauthorized levies, arrested and imprisoned; after two years judgment had not been fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Jiading Magistrate Wen Zaishang was denounced by local people for illegal levies, thrown into prison, and after two years still had no final verdict.

sentences.zh: 按察使髙承爵窮詰，在上自承嘗餽-{乾}-學子樹敏金，至事-{發}--{後}-追還，因坐樹敏罪論絞。

translations.literal: Provincial surveillance commissioner Gao Chengjue interrogated him thoroughly; Zaishang confessed that he had once presented gold to Qianxue's son Shumin, which after the matter came to light was pursued and returned; on this account Shumin was sentenced to strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial surveillance commissioner Gao Chengjue pressed the case hard; Wen confessed he had once given gold to Qianxue's son Shumin and returned it only after the affair was exposed; Shumin was therefore sentenced to strangulation.

sentences.zh: 會詔戒内外各官私怨報-{復}-，樹敏得贖罪。

translations.literal: An edict then warned all officials inside and outside against private revenge; Shumin was permitted to redeem his punishment.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then warned all officials against pursuing private vendettas, and Shumin was allowed to redeem his sentence.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，諭大學士舉長-{於}-文章學問超卓者，王熙、張玉書等-{薦}--{乾}-學與王鴻緒、髙士奇，命來京修書。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year the emperor ordered Grand Secretaries to recommend those outstanding in literary composition and learning; Wang Xi, Zhang Yushu, and others recommended Qianxue, Wang Hongxu, and Gao Shiqi, and they were ordered to come to the capital to compile books.
translations.idiomatic: In 1694 the emperor asked the Grand Secretaries to recommend scholars outstanding in letters and learning; Wang Xi and Zhang Yushu nominated Qianxue, Wang Hongxu, and Gao Shiqi, and they were summoned to Beijing to compile books.

sentences.zh: -{乾}-學已前卒，遺疎以所纂一統-{志}-進，詔下所司，-{復}-故官。

translations.literal: Qianxue had already died earlier; his posthumous memorial presented the Unified Gazetteer he had compiled; an edict was sent to the relevant offices and his former rank was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Qianxue had already died; his posthumous memorial presented the Unified Gazetteer he had compiled, and the court ordered his former rank restored.

sentences.zh: 翁叔元，字寶林，江南常熟人。

translations.literal: Weng Shuyuan, styled Baolin, was a native of Changshu in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Weng Shuyuan, whose style name was Baolin, came from Changshu in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 康熙十五年，一甲三名進士，授編修，館試第一。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Kangxi he placed third among the first-rank jinshi, was appointed compiler, and ranked first in the academy examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1676 he took third place among the top three jinshi, became a compiler, and ranked first in the Hanlin academy examination.

sentences.zh: 累遷國子監祭酒，洊擢吏部侍郎，遷工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Chancellor of the Directorate of Education, then rapidly advanced to Vice Minister of Personnel and transferred to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Chancellor of the Directorate of Education, was soon made Vice Minister of Personnel, and then Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 部例，毎有工作，先計其直上之，名曰「料估」。

translations.literal: By ministry regulation, whenever there was a project the cost was first calculated and reported upward; this was called "material estimate."
translations.idiomatic: Ministry rules required every project to have its costs estimated and reported in advance under the name "material estimate."

sentences.zh: 工完多冒破，所司不敢以聞，有十年不銷算者，大工至四十三案。

translations.literal: When work was finished there was often fraudulent overspending; the responsible offices dared not report it; some accounts were not cleared for ten years, and major projects reached forty-three cases.
translations.idiomatic: When projects ended, officials often padded expenses beyond the estimate, and the responsible offices dared not report it; some accounts remained unsettled for ten years, with as many as forty-three major projects outstanding.

sentences.zh: 叔元蒞部甫半載，積牘一淸。

translations.literal: Shuyuan had been at the ministry only half a year when the accumulated papers were all cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Within half a year of taking office Shuyuan had cleared the entire backlog.

sentences.zh: 調邢部，移疾歸，卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Ministry of Punishments, pleaded illness and returned home, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Ministry of Punishments, resigned on grounds of illness, returned home, and died.

sentences.zh: 叔元愛-{才}-而褊隘，何焯在門下，初甚賞之；

translations.literal: Shuyuan loved talent but was narrow-minded; He Chao was among his disciples and at first was greatly favored;
translations.idiomatic: Shuyuan loved talent but was narrow-minded; He Chao studied under him and was at first highly favored;

sentences.zh: 叔元疎劾湯斌，焯請削門生籍，叔元擯之，竟不得成名。

translations.literal: when Shuyuan memorialized impeaching Tang Bin, Chao asked to have his name struck from the disciples' register; Shuyuan expelled him, and he ultimately could not achieve fame.
translations.idiomatic: when Shuyuan impeached Tang Bin, He Chao asked to be struck from the register of disciples; Shuyuan cast him out, and he never achieved renown.

sentences.zh: 以是爲世所誚-{雲}-。

translations.literal: For this he was mocked by the world.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was ridiculed by contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 王鴻緒，初名度心，字季友，江南婁縣人。

translations.literal: Wang Hongxu, original name Duxin, styled Jiyou, was a native of Lou County in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hongxu, originally named Duxin and styled Jiyou, came from Lou County in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 康熙十二年一甲二名進士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Kangxi he placed second among the first-rank jinshi and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1673 he took second place among the top three jinshi and was made a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 十四年，主順天鄕試。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he presided over the Shuntian provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1675 he supervised the Shuntian provincial examinations.

sentences.zh: 充日講起居注官。

translations.literal: He served as Daily Lecturer and Recorder of the Emperor's Actions.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Daily Lecturer and Recorder of the Emperor's Actions.

sentences.zh: 累遷翰林院侍講。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Hanlin Academy Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to Lecturer in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 十九年，聖祖諭獎講官勤勞，加鴻緒侍讀學士銜。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year the Sacred Ancestor praised the lecturers' diligence and added Hongxu the title of Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: In 1680 the Kangxi Emperor commended the lecturers' diligence and granted Hongxu the rank of Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 時湖廣有硃方旦者，自號二眉山人。

translations.literal: At the time in Huguang there was Zhu Fangdan, who styled himself the Hermit of the Two Eyebrows.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Huguang had a man named Zhu Fangdan who called himself the Hermit of the Two Eyebrows.

sentences.zh: 造中説補，聚徒橫議，常至數千人。

translations.literal: He composed a Supplement to the Doctrine of the Mean, gathered disciples and held reckless discussions, often reaching several thousand people.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote a Supplement to the Doctrine of the Mean, gathered disciples, and held freewheeling public debates that often drew thousands.

sentences.zh: 自詡前知，與人決休咎。

translations.literal: He boasted of foreknowledge and for others determined fortune and misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed prophetic foresight and told people's fortunes for them.

sentences.zh: 巡撫董國興劾其左道惑衆，逮至京，得旨寬釋。

translations.literal: Governor Dong Guoxing impeached him for heterodox ways that deluded the masses; he was arrested and brought to the capital, and received an edict for lenient release.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Dong Guoxing charged him with heterodox teachings that misled the people; he was brought to Beijing but released by imperial grace.

sentences.zh: 及呉三桂反，順承郡王勒爾錦駐師荊州，方旦以佔驗出入軍營，巡撫張朝珍亦稱爲異人。

translations.literal: When Wu Sangui rebelled, Prince of the First Rank Le'erjin stationed troops at Jingzhou; Fangdan went in and out of the military camps by divination and astrology, and Governor Zhang Chaozhen also called him a wonder-worker.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui rebelled, Prince Le'erjin camped at Jingzhou; Fangdan moved freely through the camps offering divinations, and Governor Zhang Chaozhen also hailed him as a prodigy.

sentences.zh: 上密戒勒爾錦勿爲所惑。

translations.literal: The emperor secretly warned Le'erjin not to be deluded by him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor secretly warned Le'erjin not to be taken in by him.

sentences.zh: 方旦乃避走江、浙，會鴻緒得其所刊中質秘書，遂以奏進，列其誣罔君上、悖逆聖道、搖惑人心三大罪。

translations.literal: Fangdan then fled to Jiangsu and Zhejiang; Hongxu obtained his published Secret Book on the Mean in Quality and memorialized it, listing three great crimes: deceiving and misleading the ruler, rebelling against the sage Way, and unsettling people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Fangdan fled to the lower Yangtze; Hongxu obtained his published Secret Book on the Mean and presented it to the throne, charging him with deceiving the sovereign, violating the sage Way, and corrupting public morals.

sentences.zh: 方旦坐誅。

translations.literal: Fangdan was executed on conviction.
translations.idiomatic: Fangdan was put to death.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，轉侍讀，充明史總裁。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was transferred to Reader and served as chief compiler of the History of the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: In 1682 he became a Reader and chief compiler of the History of the Ming.

sentences.zh: 累擢内閣學士、戸部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand Secretariat academician and Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Grand Secretariat academician and Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，典會試。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he presided over the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1685 he served as chief examiner for the metropolitan civil service examination.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，疎請回籍治本生母喪，遣官賜祭。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he memorialized requesting return to his native place to observe mourning for his birth mother; officials were dispatched to grant sacrificial offerings.
translations.idiomatic: In 1686 he asked leave to return home to mourn his birth mother, and the court sent officials to perform the sacrificial rites.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，擢左都-{御}-史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In 1687 he was made Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 疎劾廣東巡撫李士楨貪劣，潮州知府林杭學嘗從呉三桂反，乃舉其淸廉。

translations.literal: He memorialized impeaching Guangdong Governor Li Shizhen for greed and baseness, while Chaozhou Prefect Lin Hangxue, who had once followed Wu Sangui in rebellion, he praised for purity and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Guangdong Governor Li Shizhen for corruption while praising Chaozhou Prefect Lin Hangxue—who had once joined Wu Sangui's rebellion—as incorruptible.

sentences.zh: 士楨坐罷，杭學奪職。

translations.literal: Shizhen was punished by dismissal; Hangxue was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shizhen was dismissed and Lin Hangxue was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 會靈-{臺}-郎董漢臣疎陳時事，以諭教元良、愼簡宰執爲言。

translations.literal: Astronomical Bureau director Dong Hanchen memorialized on current affairs, speaking of instructing the heir apparent and carefully selecting chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Astronomical Bureau director Dong Hanchen memorialized on current affairs, urging proper instruction for the heir apparent and careful selection of chief ministers.

sentences.zh: -{御}-史陶式玉劾漢臣摭拾浮言，欺世盜名，請逮治。

translations.literal: Censor Tao Shiyu impeached Hanchen for gathering floating words, deceiving the world and stealing reputation, and requested arrest and trial.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Tao Shiyu charged Hanchen with peddling empty talk to deceive the public and asked that he be arrested.

sentences.zh: 鴻緒疎言：「欽天監靈-{臺}-郎、博士等官，不擇流品，星-{卜}-屠沽之徒，粗識數字，便得濫竽。

translations.literal: Hongxu memorialized: "Directors and doctors of the Astronomical Bureau do not select by background; star-gazers, diviners, butchers, and peddlers who barely know characters are allowed to fill posts unworthily.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxu wrote: "The Astronomical Bureau does not screen its appointees; diviners, butchers, and peddlers who barely know their characters are allowed to hold office.

sentences.zh: 請敕下考試，分別去留。

translations.literal: I beg that an edict order examinations to separate those who stay from those who leave."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that Your Majesty order examinations to decide who should remain and who should go."

sentences.zh: 」下部議行。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the ministries and carried out.

sentences.zh: 漢臣及博士賈文然等十五人-{並}-以詞理舛誤黜。

translations.literal: Hanchen and fifteen others including Doctor Jia Wenran were all dismissed for errors in wording and reasoning.
translations.idiomatic: Hanchen and fifteen others including Doctor Jia Wenran were all dismissed for errors in their writings.

sentences.zh: 初，以式玉疎下九卿集議，尚書湯斌謂大臣不言，慚對漢臣。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shiyu's memorial was sent to the Nine Ministers for joint deliberation, Minister Tang Bin said that when great ministers do not speak out they should feel ashamed before Hanchen.
translations.idiomatic: When Tao Shiyu's memorial first went to the Nine Ministers, Minister Tang Bin said that silent ministers ought to feel ashamed before Dong Hanchen.

sentences.zh: 漢臣既黜，鴻緒偕左都-{御}-史璙丹、副都-{御}-史徐元珙合疎劾斌務名鮮實，-{並}-追論江-{寧}-巡撫去任時，巧飾文告，以博虚譽。

translations.literal: After Hanchen was dismissed, Hongxu together with Left Censor-in-Chief Lang Dan and Vice Censor-in-Chief Xu Yuanhong jointly memorialized impeaching Bin for pursuing reputation with little substance, and also pursued the matter of when he left the Jiangning governorship, artfully dressing up proclamations to win empty praise.
translations.idiomatic: After Hanchen's dismissal, Hongxu joined Left Censor-in-Chief Lang Dan and Vice Censor-in-Chief Xu Yuanhong in impeaching Tang Bin for empty reputation-mongering and for having embellished his farewell proclamations as Jiangning governor to win false praise.

sentences.zh: 上素重斌淸廉，置弗問。

translations.literal: The emperor had long valued Bin's purity and integrity and set the matter aside without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, who had long valued Tang Bin's integrity, ignored the charges.

sentences.zh: 鴻緒論各省駐防官兵累民，略言：「駐防將領恃威放肆，或占奪民業，或重息放債，或強娶民婦。

translations.literal: Hongxu discussed how garrison troops in each province burdened the people, stating in summary: "Garrison commanders rely on power and act recklessly, sometimes seizing civilians' property, sometimes lending at heavy interest, sometimes forcibly marrying civilian women.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxu memorialized on how provincial garrison troops burdened the people: "Garrison commanders abuse their power—seizing property, lending at usurious rates, or forcibly marrying local women.

sentences.zh: 或謊詐逃人，株連良善；

translations.literal: sometimes falsely accusing fugitives and implicating the innocent;
translations.idiomatic: sometimes framing fugitives and implicating the innocent;

sentences.zh: 或收羅-{姦}-棍，巧生扎詐。

translations.literal: sometimes gathering scoundrels and cunningly producing extortion;
translations.idiomatic: sometimes recruiting ruffians to extort by false accusation;

sentences.zh: -{種}--{種}-爲害，所在時有。

translations.literal: harm of every kind occurs everywhere from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: such abuses occur everywhere.

sentences.zh: 如西安、荊州駐防官兵紀律太寬，牧放馬匹，驅赴邨莊，累民芻秣；

translations.literal: For example, the garrison troops at Xi'an and Jingzhou are too lax in discipline; they pasture horses and drive them to villages, burdening the people for fodder;
translations.idiomatic: At Xi'an and Jingzhou, for example, garrison discipline is lax: horses are pastured by driving them into villages and forcing the people to supply fodder;

sentences.zh: 百十成群，踐食田禾，所至驛騷。

translations.literal: they go in groups of a hundred or ten, trampling and eating the crops, and wherever they go they cause alarm.
translations.idiomatic: they roam in bands of dozens or hundreds, trampling crops and alarming every place they pass.

sentences.zh: 其他苦累，又可類推。

translations.literal: Other hardships can be inferred by analogy.
translations.idiomatic: Other abuses may be imagined by analogy.

sentences.zh: 請嚴飭將軍、副都統等力行約束。

translations.literal: I beg that generals, vice commanders-in-chief, and others be strictly ordered to enforce restraint.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that generals and vice commanders be strictly ordered to restrain their men.

sentences.zh: 緑旗提、鎭縱兵害民，以及虚冒兵糧者，不一而足，請飭督撫立行指參。

translations.literal: Green Standard brigade and garrison commanders who indulge troops in harming the people, and those who falsely claim military rations, are more than can be counted—I beg that governors and governors-general be ordered at once to impeach specifically."
translations.idiomatic: Green Standard commanders who let their troops prey on the people and those who pad military payrolls are legion; I beg that governors be ordered to impeach them at once."

sentences.zh: 」上命議行。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the ministries to act on the proposal.

sentences.zh: 未-{幾}-，以父憂歸。

translations.literal: Before long he returned home on mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he went home to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，服闋，將赴補。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, when mourning ended, he was about to return to his post.
translations.idiomatic: In 1689, when his mourning ended, he was preparing to resume office.

sentences.zh: 左都-{御}-史郭琇劾鴻緒與髙士奇招權納賄，-{並}-及給事中何楷、編修陳元龍，皆予休致。

translations.literal: Left Censor-in-Chief Guo Xiu impeached Hongxu and Gao Shiqi for monopolizing power and accepting bribes, also implicating Supervising Secretary He Kai and Compiler Chen Yuanlong; all were granted retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Left Censor-in-Chief Guo Xiu charged Hongxu and Gao Shiqi with abusing power and taking bribes, also naming Supervising Secretary He Kai and Compiler Chen Yuanlong; all were retired.

sentences.zh: 語具士奇傳。

translations.literal: The account is given in full in Shiqi's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in Gao Shiqi's biography.

sentences.zh: 嘉定知縣聞在上爲縣民訐告私派事，按察使髙承爵按治。

translations.literal: Jiading Magistrate Wen Zaishang was impeached by county people for unauthorized levies; surveillance commissioner Gao Chengjue investigated.
translations.idiomatic: Jiading Magistrate Wen Zaishang was denounced by locals for illegal levies, and surveillance commissioner Gao Chengjue investigated.

sentences.zh: 在上言嘗以銀餽​​舉人徐樹敏，至事-{發}-退還，因坐樹敏罪。

translations.literal: Zaishang said he had once presented silver to licentiate Xu Shumin, which when the matter came to light was returned; on this account Shumin was punished.
translations.idiomatic: Wen confessed he had once given silver to licentiate Xu Shumin and returned it only after the affair was exposed; Xu Shumin was punished accordingly.

sentences.zh: 巡撫鄭端覆訊，在上言嘗以銀五百餽鴻緒，亦事-{發}-退還。

translations.literal: Governor Zheng Duan reinvestigated; Zaishang said he had once presented five hundred taels of silver to Hongxu, which was also returned when the matter came to light.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Zheng Duan reinvestigated; Wen said he had once given five hundred taels to Hongxu and had likewise returned the money after the affair was exposed.

sentences.zh: 端乃劾-{乾}-學縱子行詐，鴻緒竟染贓銀，有玷大臣名節，乞敕部嚴議。

translations.literal: Duan then impeached Qianxue for indulging his son in fraud and Hongxu for having been tainted by bribe silver, staining a great minister's reputation, and begged an edict to the ministries for severe deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng then impeached Qianxue for letting his son practice fraud and Hongxu for accepting bribe silver, disgracing ministerial rank, and asked the ministries to deliberate severely.

sentences.zh: 上特諭曰：「朕崇尚德教，蠲滌煩苛。

translations.literal: The emperor specially instructed: "We honor virtue and teaching and cleanse away troublesome severity.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued a special edict: "We honor moral teaching and seek to remove petty harshness.

sentences.zh: 凡大小臣工，-{咸}-思恩禮下逮，-{曲}-全始終；

translations.literal: All ministers great and small should think how grace and ritual reach down and how to preserve them from beginning to end;
translations.idiomatic: All officials, high and low, should remember how grace reaches down and how to preserve men from first to last;

sentences.zh: 即因事放歸，仍令各安田裡。

translations.literal: even when released home on account of affairs, they are still ordered each to settle peacefully in their fields.
translations.idiomatic: even when sent home on account of some affair, they are still allowed to live peacefully in retirement.

sentences.zh: 近見諸臣彼此傾軋，伐異黨同，私怨相尋，牽連報-{復}-；

translations.literal: Recently We have seen officials overthrowing one another, attacking the different and banding with the same, private resentments pursuing one another, implicating and retaliating;
translations.idiomatic: Lately We see officials tearing one another down, attacking rivals and forming cliques, pursuing private vendettas and retaliating by implicating others;

sentences.zh: 雖業已解職投閒，仍-{復}-吹求不已，株連逮-{於}-子弟，顛覆及-{於}-身家。

translations.literal: though already dismissed from office and living in retirement, they are still pursued without end, implicating sons and younger brothers and overturning families and persons.
translations.idiomatic: even after dismissal and retirement they are still hounded without end, implicating sons and brothers and ruining whole families.

sentences.zh: 朕總攬萬機，已三十年，此等情態，知之甚悉。

translations.literal: We have held all affairs in hand for thirty years and know such conduct very thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: We have governed for thirty years and know such conduct all too well.

sentences.zh: 媢嫉傾軋之害，歴代皆有，而明季爲甚。

translations.literal: The harm of jealousy and mutual overthrow exists in every dynasty, but was worst in the late Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Jealous factional destruction has afflicted every dynasty, but was worst in the late Ming.

sentences.zh: 公家之事，置若罔聞，而分樹黨援，飛誣排陷，迄無虚日。

translations.literal: Public affairs were treated as if unheard; factions were planted and false accusations flew in persecution without a single idle day.
translations.idiomatic: Public business was ignored while factions were built and false charges flew without a day's respite.

sentences.zh: 朕-{於}-此等背公誤國之人，深切痛恨。

translations.literal: We deeply detest such men who betray the public and harm the state.
translations.idiomatic: We deeply hate such men who betray the public interest and harm the state.

sentences.zh: 自今以往，内外大小諸臣，宜各端心-{術}-，盡蠲私忿，共矢公忠。

translations.literal: From now on, all officials inside and outside, great and small, should each rectify their hearts and methods, entirely put aside private anger, and together pledge public loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth all officials, within the court and without, should rectify their conduct, lay aside private anger, and devote themselves to public loyalty.

sentences.zh: 儻仍執迷不悟，复踵前非，朕將窮極根株，悉坐以朋黨之罪。

translations.literal: If they still cling to error and do not awaken, again following former wrongs, We will trace to the utmost roots and branches and punish all under the crime of faction.
translations.idiomatic: If they persist in error and repeat former abuses, We will trace every root and branch and punish them all for factional crime.

sentences.zh: 」時鴻緒方就質，詔至，得釋。

translations.literal: At the time Hongxu was undergoing interrogation; when the edict arrived he was released.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxu was then under interrogation; when the edict arrived he was released.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，以-{薦}-召來京修書。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he was summoned to the capital on recommendation to compile books.
translations.idiomatic: In 1694 he was summoned to Beijing on recommendation to compile books.

sentences.zh: 尋授工部尚書，充經筵講官。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Minister of Works and served as lecturer at the Classics Colloquium.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Minister of Works and lecturer at the Classics Colloquium.

sentences.zh: 四十七年，調戸部。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In 1708 he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，皇太子允礽既廢，詔大臣保奏儲貳，鴻緒與内大臣阿靈阿、侍郎揆敘等謀，舉皇子允禩，詔切責，以原品休致。

translations.literal: That winter, after the heir apparent Yinreng was deposed, an edict ordered great ministers to recommend a successor; Hongxu with inner court minister Aring'a, Vice Minister Kuixu, and others plotted to nominate Prince Yinsi; an edict sternly rebuked them and he was retired at his original rank.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, after Crown Prince Yinreng was deposed, the emperor ordered ministers to recommend a successor; Hongxu joined Inner Court Minister Aring'a and Vice Minister Kuixu in backing Prince Yinsi; the emperor sharply rebuked them and Hongxu retired at his former rank.

sentences.zh: 五十三年，疎言：「臣舊居館職，奉命爲明史總裁官，與湯斌、徐-{乾}-學、-{葉}-方靄互相參訂，僅成數巻。

translations.literal: In the fifty-third year he memorialized: "Your servant formerly held an academy post and was ordered to serve as chief compiler of the History of the Ming; together with Tang Bin, Xu Qianxue, and Ye Fang'ai he mutually revised and collated, completing only a few juan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1714 he wrote: "Your servant once held a Hanlin post and was ordered chief compiler of the History of the Ming; with Tang Bin, Xu Qianxue, and Ye Fang'ai I jointly revised the text, completing only a few juan.

sentences.zh: 及臣回籍多年，恩召重領史局，而前此纂輯諸臣，罕有存者。

translations.literal: When your servant returned to his native place for many years and was graciously summoned to head the historiography office again, of the former compilers few remained.
translations.idiomatic: After I returned home for many years Your Majesty graciously recalled me to head the historiography office, but few of the earlier compilers still survived.

sentences.zh: 惟大學士張玉書爲監修，尚書陳廷敬爲總裁，各專一類：玉書任-{志}-，廷敬任本紀，臣任列傳。

translations.literal: Only Grand Secretary Zhang Yushu served as supervising compiler and Minister Chen Tingjing as chief compiler, each specializing in one category: Yushu took the Treatises, Tingjing the Basic Annals, and your servant the Biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Only Grand Secretary Zhang Yushu supervised the project and Minister Chen Tingjing served as chief compiler, each with his specialty: Zhang the Treatises, Chen the Annals, and I the Biographies.

sentences.zh: 因臣原銜食俸，比二臣得有馀暇，刪繁就簡，正謬訂譌。

translations.literal: Because your servant retained his original rank and salary, compared with the two ministers he had more leisure to cut the redundant and keep the essential and to correct errors and emend mistakes.
translations.idiomatic: Because I kept my original rank and salary, I had more leisure than the other two to simplify the text and correct errors.

sentences.zh: 如是數年，匯分成帙，而大學士熊賜履續奉監修之命，檄取傳稿以進，玉書、廷敬暨臣皆未參閲。

translations.literal: Thus for several years the work was gathered into fascicles; then Grand Secretary Xiong Cilü again received the order to supervise compilation and requisitioned the biography drafts for submission—Yushu, Tingjing, and your servant had none of them reviewed.
translations.idiomatic: After several years the work was gathered into fascicles; then Grand Secretary Xiong Cilü, continuing as supervisor, requisitioned the biography drafts for submission without review by Zhang, Chen, or myself.

sentences.zh: 臣恐傳稿尚多舛誤，自蒙恩歸田，欲圖報稱，因重理舊編，搜殘補闕，-{復}-經五載，成列傳二百八巻。

translations.literal: Your servant feared the biography drafts still had many errors; since receiving grace to return to the fields he wished to repay it, and therefore reworked the old compilation, searching out what remained and filling gaps; after five more years he completed two hundred and eight juan of biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the drafts still contained many errors, I reworked the old compilation after returning home to repay Your Majesty's grace; after five more years I completed 208 juan of biographies.

sentences.zh: 其間是非邪正，悉據公論，不敢稍逞私臆。

translations.literal: Throughout, right and wrong, orthodox and heterodox, all followed public opinion; he did not dare indulge private judgment in the slightest.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout I followed public judgment on right and wrong and did not dare impose private opinion.

sentences.zh: 但年代久遠，傳聞異辭，未敢自信爲是。

translations.literal: But the age is remote and hearsay varies; he did not dare trust himself to be correct.
translations.idiomatic: But the events lie far in the past and reports differ, and I dare not claim certainty.

sentences.zh: 謹繕寫全稿，齎呈-{禦}--{鑑}-，請宣付史館，以備參考。

translations.literal: He respectfully copied the complete draft, presented it for imperial review, and requested that it be promulgated to the Historiography Office for reference.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully submit the complete fair copy for Your Majesty's review and ask that it be sent to the Historiography Office for reference.

sentences.zh: 」詔兪之。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the request.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，-{復}-召來京修書，充省方盛典總裁官。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year he was again summoned to the capital to compile books and served as chief compiler of the Imperial Progress Ritual Record.
translations.idiomatic: In 1715 he was again summoned to Beijing to compile books and made chief compiler of the Imperial Progress Ritual Record.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，卒-{於}-京。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he died in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Beijing in 1723.

sentences.zh: -{乾}-隆四十三年，國史館進鴻緒傳，髙宗命以郭琇劾疎載入，使-{後}-世知鴻緒輩罪狀。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year of Qianlong the National Historiography Office submitted Hongxu's biography; the Gaozong Emperor ordered that Guo Xiu's impeachment memorial be included so later generations would know Hongxu and his like's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: In 1778 the National Historiography Office submitted Hongxu's biography; the Qianlong Emperor ordered Guo Xiu's impeachment memorial included so posterity would know his crimes.

sentences.zh: 孫興吾，進士，官吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: His grandson Sun Xingwu, a jinshi, served as Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Sun Xingwu, a jinshi, became Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 髙士奇，字澹人，浙江錢塘人。

translations.literal: Gao Shiqi, styled Danren, was a native of Qiantang in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shiqi, whose style name was Danren, came from Qiantang in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 幼好學能文。

translations.literal: As a youth he loved learning and could write.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he loved learning and wrote well.

sentences.zh: 貧，以監生就順天鄕試，充書寫序班。

translations.literal: Poor, he took the Shuntian provincial examination as a student of the Imperial Academy and served as a copying orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Poor, he sat for the Shuntian provincial exams as an academy student and served as a copying clerk.

sentences.zh: 工書法，以明珠-{薦}-，入内廷供奉，授詹事府録事。

translations.literal: Skilled in calligraphy, through Songgotu's recommendation he entered the inner court as an attendant and was appointed Recorder of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in calligraphy, he entered the inner court on Songgotu's recommendation and was made Recorder of the Heir Apparent's Household.

sentences.zh: 遷内閣中書，食六品俸，賜居西安門内。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Secretariat secretary, drew sixth-rank salary, and was granted residence inside Xi'an Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He became a Grand Secretariat secretary on sixth-rank pay and was given a residence inside Xi'an Gate.

sentences.zh: 康熙十七年，聖祖降敕，以士奇書寫密諭及纂輯講章、詩文，供奉有年，特賜表裡十匹、銀五百。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Kangxi the Sacred Ancestor issued an edict: because Shiqi had for years copied secret instructions and compiled lecture chapters and literary pieces in attendance, he was specially granted ten bolts of fabric and five hundred taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: In 1678 the Kangxi Emperor issued an edict granting him ten bolts of fabric and five hundred taels of silver for years of copying secret instructions and compiling lecture texts and literary pieces at court.

sentences.zh: 十九年，复諭吏部優敘，授爲額外翰林院侍講。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he again instructed the Ministry of Personnel to give preferential promotion and appointed him extra Hanlin Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: In 1680 he again ordered the Ministry of Personnel to promote him favorably and made him an extra Hanlin Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 尋補侍讀，充日講起居注官，遷右庶子。

translations.literal: Soon he was made regular Reader, served as Daily Lecturer and Recorder of the Emperor's Actions, and was transferred to Right Sublector.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became a regular Reader, served as Daily Lecturer and Recorder of the Emperor's Actions, and was made Right Sublector.

sentences.zh: 累擢詹事府少詹事。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent's Household.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，上謁陵，-{於}-成龍在道盡-{發}-明珠、-{餘}-國柱之私。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, when the emperor visited the tombs, Yu Chenglong on the road fully exposed Songgotu and Yu Guozhu's private conduct.
translations.idiomatic: In 1687, on the emperor's tomb visit, Yu Chenglong along the route fully exposed the private misconduct of Songgotu and Yu Guozhu.

sentences.zh: 駕旋，値太皇太-{后}-喪，不入宮，以成龍言問士奇，亦盡言之。

translations.literal: When the imperial procession returned, it coincided with the Grand Empress Dowager's mourning and he did not enter the palace; using Chenglong's words he questioned Shiqi, who also told everything.
translations.idiomatic: On the return journey, during the Grand Empress Dowager's mourning the emperor did not enter the palace; he questioned Shiqi on Chenglong's report, and Shiqi told everything as well.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「何無人劾奏？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Why has no one impeached and memorialized?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Why has no one impeached them?

sentences.zh: 」士奇對曰：「人孰不畏死。

translations.literal: Shiqi replied: "Who does not fear death?"
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi replied: "Who is not afraid of death?"

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「若輩重-{於}-四輔臣乎？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Are such men weightier than the four chief ministers?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Are they more powerful than the four chief ministers?

sentences.zh: 欲去則去之矣，有何懼？

translations.literal: If one wishes to remove them, remove them—what is there to fear?"
translations.idiomatic: If I wish to remove them, I shall remove them—what is there to fear?"

sentences.zh: 」未-{幾}-，郭琇疎上，明珠、國柱遂罷相。

translations.literal: Before long Guo Xiu's memorial went up, and Songgotu and Guozhu were dismissed from the premiership.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Guo Xiu memorialized, and Songgotu and Guozhu were removed from office.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，山東巡撫張汧以齎銀赴京行賄事-{發}-，逮治，獄辭渉士奇。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year Shandong Governor Zhang Qian's matter of carrying silver to the capital to offer bribes came to light; he was arrested and tried, and the case testimony implicated Shiqi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1688 Shandong Governor Zhang Qian was arrested when his bribery mission to the capital was exposed; the case implicated Shiqi.

sentences.zh: 會奉諭戒勿株連，-{於}-是置弗問。

translations.literal: An edict had warned against implicating others; thereupon the matter was set aside without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had warned against widening the net, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 事

translations.literal: The matter
translations.idiomatic: The affair

sentences.zh: 詳徐-{乾}-學傳。

translations.literal: is given in detail in Xu Qianxue's biography.
translations.idiomatic: is recorded in detail in Xu Qianxue's biography.

sentences.zh: 士奇因疎言：「臣等編摩纂輯，惟在直廬。

translations.literal: Shiqi therefore memorialized: "Your servants compile and edit only in the direct study.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi therefore wrote: "We compile and edit only in the direct study.

sentences.zh: 宣諭奏對，悉經中使。

translations.literal: Imperial instructions and memorial replies all pass through eunuch attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial instructions and memorial replies all pass through palace eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 非進講，或數月不覲天顏，從未-{乾}-渉政事。

translations.literal: Except when lecturing, sometimes for months one does not behold the imperial countenance, and one has never interfered in government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Except when lecturing, we may go months without seeing the emperor and have never meddled in government.

sentences.zh: 不獨臣爲然，前入直諸臣，如熊賜履、-{葉}-方靄、張玉書、孫在-{豐}-、王士禎、硃彝尊等，近今同事諸臣，如陳廷敬、徐-{乾}-學、王鴻緒、張英、勵杜訥等，莫不皆然。

translations.literal: It is not only your servant; former officials on direct duty such as Xiong Cilü, Ye Fang'ai, Zhang Yushu, Sun Zaifeng, Wang Shizhen, Zhu Yizun, and recent colleagues such as Chen Tingjing, Xu Qianxue, Wang Hongxu, Zhang Ying, and Li Dun'e—none were otherwise.
translations.idiomatic: This is true not only of me but of all who have served in the direct study, from Xiong Cilü, Ye Fang'ai, Zhang Yushu, Sun Zaifeng, Wang Shizhen, and Zhu Yizun in earlier times to Chen Tingjing, Xu Qianxue, Wang Hongxu, Zhang Ying, and Li Dun'e in our own day.

sentences.zh: 獨是供奉日久，嫌疑日滋。

translations.literal: Only because attendance has been long, suspicion grows daily.
translations.idiomatic: Only because I have served so long, suspicion has grown daily.

sentences.zh: 張汧無端疑怨，含沙汚衊，臣將無以自明，幸賴聖明在上，誣構難施。

translations.literal: Zhang Qian bears groundless suspicion and resentment, casting sand to slander and defile; your servant would have no way to clear himself, but fortunately relying on the sage clarity above, false framing cannot be applied.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qian bears me groundless malice and slanders me with hidden arrows; I could not clear myself but for Your Majesty's clarity, which prevents false charges from succeeding.

sentences.zh: 但禁廷淸秘，來茲萋斐，豈容仍玷淸班？

translations.literal: But the forbidden court is pure and secret; if slander comes hereafter, how can one still stain the pure ranks?
translations.idiomatic: But the inner court is pure and secret; how can I remain in the pure service if slander continues?

sentences.zh: 伏乞賜歸田裡。

translations.literal: I humbly beg to be granted return to my fields."
translations.idiomatic: I beg leave to return home."

sentences.zh: 」上命解任，仍領修書事。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered him relieved of office but still to head book compilation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor relieved him of office but kept him in charge of book compilation.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，從上南巡，至杭州，幸士奇西溪山莊，-{御}-書「竹窗」榜額賜之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he accompanied the emperor on the southern tour; at Hangzhou the emperor visited Shiqi's Xixi mountain villa and granted an imperial inscription reading "Bamboo Window" as a plaque.
translations.idiomatic: In 1689, on the southern tour, the emperor visited Shiqi's villa at Xixi near Hangzhou and bestowed an imperial plaque inscribed "Bamboo Window."

sentences.zh: 未-{幾}-，左都-{御}-史郭琇劾奏曰：「皇上宵旰焦勞，勵精圖治，用人行政，未嘗-{纖}-毫假手左右。

translations.literal: Before long, Left Censor-in-Chief Guo Xiu impeached and memorialized, saying: "The emperor labors early and late in anxious toil, striving with vigor to bring order; in appointing men and administering affairs, he has never entrusted even the slightest matter to those at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Left Censor-in-Chief Guo Xiu submitted an impeachment memorial: "Your Majesty rises early and sleeps late in anxious labor, striving to govern well, and in appointing officials and conducting policy You have never entrusted even the smallest matter to those around You.

sentences.zh: 乃有原任少詹事髙士奇、左都-{御}-史王鴻緒等，表-{里}-爲-{姦}-，植黨營私，試略陳其罪。

translations.literal: Yet there are the former Junior Guardian Gao Shiqi, Left Censor-in-Chief Wang Hongxu, and others, who inside and outside act as villains, planting factions and pursuing private gain—your servant will briefly set forth their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Yet former Junior Guardian Gao Shiqi, Left Censor-in-Chief Wang Hongxu, and their associates collude inside and outside to do evil, forming factions and seeking private profit; I will briefly set forth their crimes.

sentences.zh: 士奇出身微賤，其始徒歩來京，覓館爲生。

translations.literal: Shiqi came from humble origins; at first he walked to the capital and found employment as a tutor to make a living.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi came from humble origins; at first he walked to the capital and supported himself by teaching in private studios.

sentences.zh: 皇上因其字學頗工，不拘資格，擢補翰林。

translations.literal: Because his calligraphy was quite accomplished, the emperor, not bound by seniority, promoted him to the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Impressed by his accomplished calligraphy, the emperor waived normal qualifications and appointed him to the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 令入南書房供奉，不過使之考訂文章，原未假之與聞政事。

translations.literal: He was ordered to serve in the Southern Studio; this was no more than having him collate and revise texts, and originally he was not entrusted to hear of or participate in government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned to serve in the Southern Studio, where his duties were only to edit and revise texts; he was never meant to share in governance.

sentences.zh: 而士奇日思結納，諂附大臣，攬事招權，以圖分肥。

translations.literal: Yet Shiqi daily thought of forming connections, flattering and attaching himself to great ministers, seizing affairs and inviting power in order to share the spoils.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Shiqi daily schemed to cultivate connections, fawning on senior ministers, grabbing authority and gathering power so he could share in the spoils.

sentences.zh: 内外大小臣工，無不知有士奇者。

translations.literal: Officials great and small, inside and outside, none fail to know of Shiqi.
translations.idiomatic: Officials throughout the court and the provinces all know who Shiqi is.

sentences.zh: 聲名赫奕，乃至如此。

translations.literal: His fame resounds so brilliantly—it has reached this point.
translations.idiomatic: His renown has grown to such eminence.

sentences.zh: 是其罪之可誅者一也。

translations.literal: This is the first of his crimes deserving execution.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first crime for which he deserves punishment.

sentences.zh: 久之羽翼既多，遂自立門戸，結王鴻緒爲死黨，給事中何楷爲義兄弟，翰林陳元龍爲叔侄，鴻緒兄頊齡爲子女姻親，倶寄以心腹，在外招攬。

translations.literal: After long time his wings and talons were many; he then established his own faction, binding Wang Hongxu as a sworn partisan, Supervising Secretary He Kai as sworn brother, Hanlin Academician Chen Yuanlong as uncle and nephew, and Hongxu's elder brother Xuling as marriage kin for their children—all entrusted as trusted agents to recruit followers outside.
translations.idiomatic: In time, once he had built up a large following, he set up his own faction: Wang Hongxu became his sworn ally; Supervising Secretary He Kai, his sworn brother; Hanlin Academician Chen Yuanlong, his partner in a fabricated uncle-nephew tie; and Hongxu's elder brother Xuling, linked by their children's marriages. He trusted them all as inner agents to recruit supporters in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 凡督、撫、籓、臬、道、府、廳、縣及在内大小卿員，皆鴻緒、楷等爲之居停，哄騙餽至，成千累萬。

translations.literal: All governors-general, governors, feudal nobles, provincial judges, circuit intendants, prefects, sub-prefects, magistrates, and great and small ministers within—all were served by Hongxu, Kai, and the rest as go-betweens; deceived gifts arrived amounting to tens of thousands upon tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Every governor-general, governor, noble, provincial judge, circuit intendant, prefect, sub-prefect, magistrate, and senior official at court had Hongxu, He Kai, and the others acting as brokers for them; gifts obtained by deception piled up to tens and hundreds of thousands.

sentences.zh: 即不屬黨護者，亦有常例，名之曰'平安錢'。

translations.literal: Even those not belonging to their faction still had a standing custom, called 'peace money.'
translations.idiomatic: Even officials outside their faction paid a regular tribute they called 'peace money'—a bribe for safety.

sentences.zh: 是士奇等之-{姦}-貪壞法，全無顧忌，其罪之可誅者二也。

translations.literal: Thus Shiqi and his associates' villainous greed and violation of law show absolutely no scruple—this is the second crime deserving execution.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Shiqi and his associates' corrupt law-breaking knows no restraint; this is the second punishable crime.

sentences.zh: 光棍兪子易，在京肆橫有年，事-{發}-潛遁。

translations.literal: The ruffian Yu Ziyi had for years run rampant in the capital; when the affair was exposed he fled in secret.
translations.idiomatic: The thug Yu Ziyi had bullied his way through the capital for years; when the affair came to light he fled.

sentences.zh: 有虎坊橋瓦房六十馀間，-{價}-値八千金，餽送士奇。

translations.literal: He had more than sixty tile-roofed houses at Tiger Bridge, worth eight thousand taels of gold, which were sent as gifts to Shiqi.
translations.idiomatic: He owned more than sixty tiled houses at Hufang Bridge, worth eight thousand taels, and presented them to Shiqi.

sentences.zh: 此外順成門外斜街-{並}-各處房屋，令心腹出名置買，寄頓賄銀至四十馀萬。

translations.literal: Besides these, at Slanting Street outside Shuncheng Gate and at various places, he had trusted agents purchase property in their own names, storing bribe silver up to more than four hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In addition, on Slanting Street outside Shuncheng Gate and at other locations, he had agents buy property in their own names and deposited more than four hundred thousand taels of bribe money.

sentences.zh: 又-{於}-本鄕平湖縣置田産千頃，大興土木，杭州西溪廣置園宅。

translations.literal: Further, in his native Pinghu County he acquired a thousand qing of land and undertook great construction; at Xixi in Hangzhou he extensively bought gardens and mansions.
translations.idiomatic: He also amassed a thousand qing of land in his native Pinghu County and built lavishly; at Xixi near Hangzhou he acquired extensive estates.

sentences.zh: 以覓館餬口之窮儒，忽爲數百萬之富翁。

translations.literal: A poor scholar who scraped a living finding studios suddenly became a millionaire worth several million.
translations.idiomatic: A poor scholar who once barely made ends meet by tutoring suddenly became a man worth millions.

sentences.zh: 試問金從何來？

translations.literal: May one ask: whence came the gold?
translations.idiomatic: Whence came this wealth?

sentences.zh: 無非取給-{於}-各官。

translations.literal: Nothing but taken and supplied from the various officials.
translations.idiomatic: It all came from the officials.

sentences.zh: 官從何來？

translations.literal: Whence came the officials' [wealth]?
translations.idiomatic: And whence came their wealth?

sentences.zh: 非侵國帑，即剝民膏。

translations.literal: If not embezzling the state treasury, then flaying the people's fat.
translations.idiomatic: Either from embezzling the state treasury or from squeezing the people dry.

sentences.zh: 是士奇等眞國之蠹而民之賊也，其罪之可誅者三也。

translations.literal: Thus Shiqi and his associates are truly vermin of the state and robbers of the people—this is the third crime deserving execution.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi and his associates are truly parasites on the state and plunderers of the people; this is the third punishable crime.

sentences.zh: 皇上洞悉其罪，因各館編纂未竣，令解任修書，矜全之恩至矣！

translations.literal: The emperor thoroughly understood their crimes, but because compilation in the various bureaus was not finished, ordered them relieved of office to compile books—the grace of sparing and preserving them was utmost!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty saw through their crimes, yet because the various compilation projects were unfinished, You relieved them of office while letting them continue the books—a mercy beyond measure!

sentences.zh: 士奇不思改過自新，仍怙惡不悛，當聖駕南巡，上諭嚴戒餽送，以軍法治罪。

translations.literal: Shiqi did not think to reform and renew himself, but still clung to evil without repentance; when the sacred carriage toured south, the emperor issued instructions strictly forbidding gifts and threatening military-law punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi did not repent; he persisted in evil. When the imperial tour went south, Your Majesty strictly forbade gift-giving and warned that military law would punish violators.

sentences.zh: 惟士奇與鴻緒愍不畏死，鴻緒在淮、揚等處，招攬各官餽送萬金，潛遺士奇。

translations.literal: Only Shiqi and Hongxu still showed no fear of death; Hongxu in Huaiyang and other places recruited officials' gifts of ten thousand gold pieces and secretly sent them to Shiqi.
translations.idiomatic: Only Shiqi and Hongxu dared defy death itself: in the Huai-Yang region and elsewhere, Hongxu solicited gifts of ten thousand taels from officials and secretly forwarded them to Shiqi.

sentences.zh: 淮、揚如此，他處可知。

translations.literal: If Huai and Yang are thus, other places may be inferred.
translations.idiomatic: If this happened in Huai and Yangzhou, one knows what occurred elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 是士奇等欺君滅法，背公行私，其罪之可誅者四也。

translations.literal: Thus Shiqi and his associates deceive the ruler and extinguish the law, betraying public duty for private ends—this is the fourth crime deserving execution.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi and his associates deceived the throne and defied the law, betraying public duty for private ends; this is the fourth punishable crime.

sentences.zh: 王鴻緒、陳元龍鼎甲出身，儼然士林翹楚；

translations.literal: Wang Hongxu and Chen Yuanlong came from top triennial examination ranks, loftily the leading figures of the scholar-official world;
