translations.idiomatic: Wang Hongxu and Chen Yuanlong were top examination graduates, eminent leaders among scholar-officials;

sentences.zh: 竟不顧淸議，依媚大臣，無所不至。

translations.literal: yet they utterly disregard pure opinion, relying on and flattering great ministers, to every extreme.
translations.idiomatic: yet they brushed aside public reproach and fawned on powerful ministers without limit.

sentences.zh: 苟圖富貴，傷敗名教，豈不玷朝班而羞當世之士哉？

translations.literal: If only pursuing wealth and honor, injuring and corrupting the teaching of names and rites—do they not stain the court ranks and shame the scholars of the age?
translations.idiomatic: Scheming only for wealth and rank, they have corrupted the moral order—do they not disgrace the court and shame their contemporaries?

sentences.zh: 總之髙士奇、王鴻緒、陳元龍、何楷、王頊齡等，豺狼其性，蛇蠍其心，鬼蜮其形。

translations.literal: In sum, Gao Shiqi, Wang Hongxu, Chen Yuanlong, He Kai, Wang Xuling, and the rest—wolfish and jackal in nature, viperous in heart, demonic and treacherous in form.
translations.idiomatic: In sum, Gao Shiqi, Wang Hongxu, Chen Yuanlong, He Kai, Wang Xuling, and the rest are wolves and jackals by nature, serpents in heart, and demons in deed.

sentences.zh: 畏勢者既觀望而不敢言，趨勢者-{復}-擁戴而不肯言。

translations.literal: Those who fear power already look on and dare not speak; those who court power again embrace and uphold them and will not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Those who fear their power watch in silence; those who chase their power rally behind them and refuse to speak out.

sentences.zh: 臣若不言，有負聖恩。

translations.literal: If your servant does not speak, he fails the sacred grace.
translations.idiomatic: If I remain silent, I fail Your Majesty's grace.

sentences.zh: 故不避嫌怨，請立賜罷斥，明正典刑，天下幸甚。

translations.literal: Therefore not avoiding resentment and suspicion, your servant begs that they immediately be dismissed and expelled, clearly applying the statutory punishment—great fortune for all under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: I therefore set aside fear of reprisal and beg that they be dismissed at once and punished according to law—for the good of the realm."

sentences.zh: 」疎入，士奇等倶休致回籍。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, Shiqi and the others were all granted retirement and sent to their native places.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Shiqi and the others were all retired and sent home.

sentences.zh: 副都-{御}-史許三禮复疎劾解任尚書徐-{乾}-學與士奇姻親，招搖納賄，相爲表裡。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Xu Sanli again memorialized in impeachment that the relieved-of-office Minister Xu Qianxue was related by marriage to Shiqi, swaggered and accepted bribes, and acted inside and outside with each other.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Xu Sanli submitted another impeachment charging that the dismissed Minister Xu Qianxue, who was related to Shiqi by marriage, swaggered about accepting bribes and worked inside and outside in collusion with him.

sentences.zh: 部議以所劾無據，得寢。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated that the impeached charges lacked evidence, and the matter was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry found the charges unsupported, and the case was dropped.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，召來京修書。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he was summoned to the capital to compile books.
translations.idiomatic: In 1694 he was summoned to Beijing to compile books.

sentences.zh: 士奇既至，仍直南書房。

translations.literal: Once Shiqi arrived, he again served on duty in the Southern Studio.
translations.idiomatic: When Shiqi arrived, he again served in the Southern Studio.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，以養母乞歸，詔允之，特授詹事府詹事。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year, citing care for his mother, he begged to return home; an edict granted it, and he was specially appointed Grand Preceptor in the Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In 1697 he asked leave to return home to care for his mother; the emperor granted it and specially appointed him Grand Preceptor in the Household of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 尋擢禮部侍郎，以母老未赴。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites, but because his mother was elderly he did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Vice Minister of Rites but did not take up the appointment because his mother was elderly.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，上南巡，士奇迎駕淮安，扈蹕至杭州。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year the emperor toured south; Shiqi met the imperial carriage at Huai'an and accompanied the procession to Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1703, on the southern tour, Shiqi met the emperor at Huai'an and accompanied the procession to Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 及回鑾，-{復}-從至京師，屢入對，賜予優渥。

translations.literal: When the imperial return was complete, he again followed to the capital; he repeatedly entered for audience, receiving generous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: On the return journey he followed the emperor to the capital, was received in audience many times, and received lavish rewards.

sentences.zh: 上顧侍臣曰：「朕初讀書，内監授以四子本經，作時文；

translations.literal: The emperor looked at the attending ministers and said: "When I first studied, eunuchs taught me the Four Books in standard editions and how to compose examination essays;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to his attendants: "When I first studied, eunuchs taught me the Four Books and examination essay writing;

sentences.zh: 得士奇，始知學問門徑。

translations.literal: when I obtained Shiqi, I first knew the gateway to learning.
translations.idiomatic: only when I met Shiqi did I learn the true path of scholarship.

sentences.zh: 初見士奇得古人詩文，一覽即知其時代，心以爲異，未-{幾}-，朕亦能之。

translations.literal: At first when Shiqi obtained ancient men's poetry and prose, with one glance he knew their era; the heart took it for strange—before long, I could do so as well.
translations.idiomatic: At first I marveled that Shiqi could tell at a glance the period of any classical poem or essay; before long I could do the same.

sentences.zh: 士奇無戰陣功，而朕待之厚，以其裨朕學問者大也。

translations.literal: Shiqi has no battle and formation merit, yet I treat him generously because his aid to my learning is great."
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi won no military distinction, yet I have treated him generously because he has greatly advanced my learning."

sentences.zh: 」尋遣歸，是年卒-{於}-家。

translations.literal: Soon he was sent home, and that year he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was sent home, and that year he died there.

sentences.zh: 上深惜之，命加給全葬，授其子庶吉士輿爲編修。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply regretted it, ordered additional full funeral provision, and appointed his son, Hanlin probationer Yu, as Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply mourned his loss, ordered a full state funeral subsidy, and appointed his son Yu, then a Hanlin probationer, as Compiler.

sentences.zh: 尋諡文恪。

translations.literal: Soon he was posthumously titled Wenke.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given the posthumous title Wenke.

sentences.zh: 論曰：儒臣直内廷，謂之「書房」，存未入關前舊名也。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Confucian ministers serving directly in the inner court are called the 'Study'—preserving the old name from before entering the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: Scholar-officials on direct duty in the inner court were called the 'Study,' preserving a pre-conquest name.

sentences.zh: 上書房授諸皇子讀，尊爲師傅；

translations.literal: The Eastern Study instructs the imperial princes in reading and is honored as tutor;
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Study taught the imperial princes and was held in honor as their teachers;

sentences.zh: 南書房以詩文書畫供-{禦}-，地分淸切，參與密勿。

translations.literal: the Southern Study supplies poetry, prose, calligraphy, and painting for the emperor; its position is pure and close, participating in confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: the Southern Study provided poetry, calligraphy, and painting for the emperor; its station was exalted and intimate, and it shared in secret deliberations.

sentences.zh: -{乾}-學、士奇先-{後}-入直，鴻緒亦以文學進。

translations.literal: Qianxue and Shiqi entered direct duty in succession; Hongxu also advanced through literary accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Qianxue and Shiqi entered direct service in turn, and Hongxu also rose through literary talent.

sentences.zh: 乃憑藉權勢，互結黨援，納賄營私，致屢遭彈劾，聖祖-{曲}-予保全。

translations.literal: Yet relying on power and influence, they mutually formed factional ties, accepted bribes and pursued private gain, causing repeated impeachment; the Sacred Ancestor graciously preserved them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they relied on power, formed factions, took bribes, and pursued private gain, drawing repeated impeachment—and still the Kangxi Emperor mercifully spared them.

sentences.zh: -{乾}-學、鴻緒猶得以書局自隨，竟編纂之業，士奇亦以恩禮終，不其幸歟！

translations.literal: Qianxue and Hongxu could still take the book bureau with them and completed the compilation work; Shiqi also ended with imperial favor and ceremony—are they not fortunate!
translations.idiomatic: Xu Qianxue and Wang Hongxu still kept their compilation duties and finished their editorial work; Shiqi too died with imperial honor—were they not fortunate indeed!
